Sephirotic Scion. Your blood remembers the higher spheres. Light hangs around you a little too long, prayers sometimes answer themselves, and the world’s moral architecture feels less like an abstraction and more like the weather report.

Sephirotic Scion Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Sephirotic).

  • Size. You are Medium.

  • Speed. Your walking speed is 6 squares

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Sephirotic Scion does not grant any attribute bonuses.

Your Sephirotic heritage grants you additional features through advancements (Item Grants) added during character creation: sephirotic physiology, attunement to higher patterns, holy conduction, the Light of Harmony, and strategic hooks that tilt factions toward soft power, diplomacy, and alignment work.

Bad Eden Heritage (v1.1, RFI-native). Sephirotic Scion heritage: Ophanic.

“The wheels were full of eyes. You never stop turning. You never stop seeing.”

Sephirotic Scion (Ophanic). Your blood runs rotating. The Ophanim are wheels-and-eyes — motion, sight, the order that is always already looking both ways. You are descended from a thing that could not be snuck up on because it had no back. You kept some of that. Not all. Enough.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Sephirotic Scion).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Movement. 6 squares walking.

  • Lineage Lean. Sephirotic Scion does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Intrigue in fiction and through Tier powers.

Sephirotic Scion Core: The Higher Register

Shared across all Sephirotic Scion heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Sephirotic Physiology. You have resistance to sephirotic damage. Your blood runs a little bright under the right light; you do not technically age while on consecrated ground.

  • Sefirot Attunement. At creation, pick one sephirah (player choice). Once per scene, you can invoke its register and gain a +1 rank bonus to one check that falls clearly within that sephirah's domain.

  • Holy Conduit. Manifestations, rituals, and other sephirotic-register effects that target you or pass through your space treat their effective caster-attribute as +1 for the duration of that effect. Works on allies and on you; does not work on qliphothic-register effects.

  • Light of Harmony. When two or more creatures within 6 squares of you are in active, explicit agreement (stated aloud), they each gain 1 temporary Integrity. This refreshes when a new agreement is reached between different creatures.

Ophanic Traits

  • Wheel-and-Eye. You can see invisible creatures and objects within 6 squares as dimly lit shapes. You cannot be flanked.

  • Concentric Sight. You reroll the lowest die on Mind (Perception) checks that involve noticing movement, pattern, or change over time. You roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Mind (Perception) checks to notice things that have been perfectly still since before you started looking — you see motion, not furniture.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

  • OP Edge. Your faction gains +2 Intrigue OP and +1 Violence OP at campaign start.

  • Hex Synergy. In Battlefield / Procession / High-Traffic hexes, your faction's observation and counter-intel operations gain +2 on the success check.

  • Turning Witness. Once per Strategic Turn, you may observe one exchange of goods, intelligence, or personnel between two rival factions within your field of influence. You learn that it happened and between whom, though not necessarily what was exchanged.

description.value:
Primary Attribute: Presence

Every manifestation is an agreement with something. Most casters don't read what they signed. You did, you do, and you keep what you signed for.

Manifestation Discipline: Upkeep / concurrency specialist (5-pt budget — Upkeep ●●●, Misfire ●●, Clarity ●, Reach ●, Signature Mode: Sealed Pact)

Class Identity

Tier cap and footprint stay universal. What you have is holding: more concurrent manifestations sustained at once, lower upkeep on bargained subjects, and the right to renegotiate a misfire instead of eating it. Steward still out-mythics you on scope. Pactkeepers don't manifest bigger — they manifest more, longer, and in writing.

Class Features

  • Initiation 1 — The Bargain. The Pact slot comes online (existing class resource — see your Doctrine for the generation / tier rule). While a creature, object, or place is bargained-with as your Pact subject, you may sustain one additional manifestation on or near them at no extra upkeep against your Clarity. Skill rank +1 in two of: Diplomacy, Insight, Intimidation, Lore.
  • Initiation 6 — Renegotiate. When one of your manifestations would misfire, you may instead accept a GM-set narrative debt (a future scene, a future cost, a future favor owed) and treat the manifestation as having succeeded at base tier. The debt is real; the GM's table runs the bill.
  • Initiation 11 — Sealed Pact (Signature Mode). Stance. While the Seal holds, your concurrent-manifestation cap is +2, and you cannot voluntarily drop a manifestation sustained on a pact-bound subject (the seal carries the upkeep, not your moment-to-moment will). Pays ongoing upkeep against your Clarity. (Pilot: lock exact upkeep curve and break condition after one playtest cycle.)
  • Initiation 16 — Ledger Day. 1/Soma Break, transfer one of your sustained manifestations to a willing ally — they pick up upkeep from their Clarity from that point on. The pact moves with the paper, not the person who originally signed.

Doctrines

See your Doctrine document for the L1 Pact slot generation rule and the rest of the doctrine ladder. Doctrines remain the depth lane — the Discipline budget above is what you bring to any Pact-shape.

Carryover Notes

  • Existing Pact / pool mechanics are preserved; concurrency-bonus above stacks with pool spend, not a replacement.
  • Tier cap, footprint, Clarity max are universal. Holding power is the only knob you bend.

“Reality is consistent because someone keeps the minutes.”

Administrative Pressure: +3

You are licensed to administer continuity of meaning: what counts as having happened, how strongly the past pulls on the present, and which version of events becomes official.

Esoteric Bias: Divination (Chokhmah) and Illusion (Hod). When casting manifestations from these schools, misalignment penalties are suppressed; aligned casting generates +1 Civic Charge.

Always Prepared Manifestations: Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth, Clairvoyance, Modify Memory, Legend Lore.

Unique Contract: Binding Precedent (see Pactkeeper features).

🧭 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Jurisdiction

Type: Permanent class feature (Level 1)
Purpose: Defines what you are authorized to administer

A Jurisdiction does not grant power directly.
It grants permission.

What Jurisdiction Does

Your Jurisdiction determines:

  • Which situations generate Civic Charge more easily

  • Which effects you may enforce without Pressure

  • Which Contracts you can issue by default

  • Which manifestations are considered “in mandate”

Example:

  • A Steward acting on community morale = in mandate

  • A Steward issuing divine sanctions = out of mandate (Pressure risk)

Jurisdiction Is NOT:

  • A resource pool

  • A bonus to rolls

  • A manifestation list restriction

It is a scope limiter and Pressure filter.
Administrative Pressure measures the bureaucratic and metaphysical strain you generate by making reality hold still.
Civic Charge is permission, credibility, and stabilizing authority made spendable. This is your display item for current Civic Charge and Administrative Pressure on the Features tab.

“This happened. It matters. Act accordingly.”

When a significant action succeeds or fails, you may establish a Precedent tied to a creature, location, faction, or concept. While active, similar future actions reroll the lowest die if aligned with the precedent, or suffer disadvantage if they violate it. You are not forcing outcomes—you are making contradiction expensive.

Precedent is probability gravity, not mind control.

“Godhood is community service. I’m here to keep the lights on.”

Manifesting (Delegated): You are a full prepared caster. Your manifesting is routed through stabilized civic thoughtforms (tulpas), retired gods, and the Long Quiet—reducing volatility and preventing raw backlash.

Civic Charge: You maintain a pool of Civic Charge used to cite precedent, stabilize outcomes, and enforce contracts. Your subclass and Jurisdiction determine how you gain and spend it.

Delegated Channeling: When you cast a manifestation, you treat esoteric misalignment as neutral (no penalty). When you cast in alignment with your Jurisdiction, you convert alignment into resources rather than raw power.

🟣 PACTKEEPER — CORE MECHANICS

🗂 CLASS RESOURCE: Civic Charge

Type: Dice-based resource pool
Purpose: Represents institutional authority, social mandate, and metaphysical clearance

Civic Charge Dice

  • Start as d6

  • Increase at:

    • Level 5 → d8

    • Level 11 → d10

    • Level 17 → d12

  • Maximum stored dice:
    = your Soul modifier (minimum 1)

You cannot store Civic Charge beyond this limit.

Gaining Civic Charge

You gain 1 Civic Charge Die when any one of the following occurs:

  • You successfully stabilize a volatile situation
    (panic, corruption, escalation, social collapse)

  • You resolve a conflict without increasing Violence

  • You enforce a binding Contract or Precedent

  • You complete a meaningful ritual, mediation, or closure action

  • You cast a manifestation in esoteric alignment (correct correspondence / timing)

Limit:
You may gain only 1 Civic Charge Die per round.

Spending Civic Charge

When you spend a Civic Charge Die, roll it and apply the result as one of the following:

  • Stabilization: Reduce incoming damage, panic, corruption, or fallout by the rolled amount

  • Authority Boost: Add the rolled value to a manifestation DC, contested roll, or enforcement check

  • Enforcement: Force a reroll against a Contract or Precedent (target takes the worse result)

  • Containment: Convert a catastrophic outcome into a controlled one

  • Closure: End an ongoing effect cleanly instead of explosively

Each use consumes the die.

Running Out of Civic Charge

If you have 0 Civic Charge Dice:

  • You may still cast manifestations and use features

  • But you cannot:

    • Enforce contracts

    • Prevent escalation

    • Convert failures into clean outcomes

You are now acting without mandate, which invites pushback.

⚖ PUSHBACK SYSTEM: Administrative Pressure

Pactkeepers do not suffer backlash.
They accumulate Administrative Pressure.

You gain Pressure when:

  • You act outside your Jurisdiction

  • You override community consent

  • You force outcomes repeatedly

  • You ignore due process or precedent

Effects of Pressure (GM-facing bands)

  • Low: NPCs question authority, cooperation drops

  • Moderate: Enforcement costs increase, resistance grows

  • High: Mandates contested, Auditors intervene, Jurisdiction narrows

Pressure Points

Administrative Pressure is tracked as points, not just bands.

  • Low: 1–2 Pressure
  • Moderate: 3–5 Pressure
  • High: 6+ Pressure

Pressure is still narrative, but these thresholds provide a visible meter for play.

Clearing Pressure

  • Downtime

  • Proper closure

  • Delegation to other systems

  • Subclass features (Steward, Decommissioner especially)

Pressure is narrative, but persistent.

“I’m citing case law.”

Administrative Pressure: −2

Spend Civic Charge to invoke the record:

  • Cite Precedent: Force a reroll by asserting consistency. If the action violates an established precedent, the reroll takes the worse result.
  • Establish Record: Lock an outcome as official for purposes of consequence and precedent.
  • Suppress Contradiction: Nullify paradox, contradictory magic, or narrative retcons for one moment.
  • 📑

📑 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Precedent

Type: Persistent world state marker
Purpose: Makes outcomes stick and repetition matter

Precedents are not dice. They are flags on reality.

Creating a Precedent

A Precedent is created when:

  • A major action succeeds or fails

  • A Contract is enforced

  • A significant moral or political line is crossed

  • A Pactkeeper explicitly declares one (Archivist specialty)

What a Precedent Does

While active, a Precedent causes:

  • Repeated similar actions to:

    • Suffer disadvantage, or

    • Trigger automatic consequences

  • NPCs and systems to “expect” consistency

  • Reality to resist contradiction

Interacting with Precedent

Pactkeepers may spend Civic Charge to:

  • Cite a Precedent (force rerolls)

  • Lock an outcome as official

  • Suppress contradictory magic or retcons

Archivists gain expanded control over this.

Ending a Precedent

A Precedent ends when:

  • It is superseded

  • It is resolved narratively

  • It is formally revoked

  • A Decommissioner retires it

Spend 1 Civic Charge and open the Pactkeeper action dialog.

  • Stabilization
  • Authority Boost
  • Enforcement
  • Containment
  • Closure

Every ruling has already been made. I know where.

Mode: Historical enforcement / drift: Toward

Level 1: Read The Ledger

You are trained in a vast internal catalog of historical rulings, treaties, precedents, and case records spanning the setting's known Lore. At character creation and on each a Soma Break, you may prepare [TBD:balance — Soul mod] Precedents — specific historical rulings relevant to situations you anticipate encountering. When a prepared Precedent becomes relevant in play, you may invoke it as an action, spending [TBD:balance — 2 Leverage] to compel the current situation to resolve under its terms. GM adjudicates fit.

Level 5: Citation In Hand

Once per scene, you may invoke a Precedent that you did not prepare, if you can plausibly know it (GM judgment). Treat this as a Precedent invocation at +1 Leverage cost. The fact that an Archivist can produce a citation at any moment makes opposing legal positions significantly less stable, which is the actual game-state effect.

Level 9: Binding Lineage

When you invoke a Precedent in a political proceeding (faction-level dispute, hex-level governance, contract negotiation), the outcome is treated as continuing the line — it counts as an additional entry in the historical record for future invocations. You and any Archivist after you may invoke the present ruling as Precedent in future cases, making your in-play decisions genuinely load-bearing for the setting's legal Lore.

Level 13: The Unbroken Chain

You may declare a Chain of Precedent — a series of three or more historical rulings that, taken together, compel a specific outcome in the current situation. Chains are invoked as a single action for [TBD:balance — 8 Leverage]. The target of the Chain (a creature, faction, or ongoing effect) must make a Soul check [TBD:balance DC] or be bound by the Chain's implied ruling. Binding effects last until the ruling is formally appealed or overturned.

Level 17: The Standing Record (Capstone)

You may declare a Precedent of your own at the end of a session — a ruling that the events of the session establish as binding going forward. The Precedent is permanent unless overturned by the session's recognized authority. From this point forward, you and future Pactkeepers may invoke this Precedent in play. Over a campaign, the Archivist of Precedent accumulates a body of personal case law that reshapes the setting's legal landscape.

“Everything connects. Including you.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The World (Integrator). You see systems as wholes. Supply, ritual, morale, politics, travel, violence, myth — to you, these are not separate tracks, but one machine with many faces.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype strengthens cross-system alignment and broad operational cohesion. This Archetype is associated with +1 Economy and +1 Diplomacy in faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit.

Beauty - Balance that costs something. +1 Diplomacy, +1 Soft Power OPs

Tiphareth holds justice and mercy in living tension. It rewards balanced play, stability across multiple systems, and factions that survive by integrating contradictions instead of denying them.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Exorcist / Purifier.

“You don’t negotiate with the darkness. You end it.”

Exorcists do not bargain. They do not reinterpret. They do not accept corruption as a usable state.

To an Exorcist, the Great Work is not about managing the broken world. It is about removing what should not be there and restoring the conditions under which something honest can exist again.

Where Goetics bind, Exorcists sever. Where Shamans listen, Exorcists intervene. Where Kabbalists align, Exorcists cleanse.

How Exorcists pursue the Great Work:

  • By removing Qliphothic influence and corruption
  • By stabilizing Hexes under Darkness pressure
  • By preventing the spread of systemic decay
  • By refusing to let harmful systems persist just because they are useful

Resonance: Tiferet / Purity — clarity, balance, and the reassertion of what should be.

Tell-tales: still air where there should be movement, silence after tension, things that stop being wrong without explanation.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 specialty edge on actions involving stabilization, cleansing, or anti-corruption pressure

Cost Principle: removal is violent in its own way. Expect rigidity, collateral suppression, and consequences when something removed turns out to have been holding something worse in place.

Crew Type (Bad Eden): Ironbound Ascendants.

“Height is not terrain. It is policy.”

Ironbound Ascendants make strongholds out of bad footing and turn cliffs into arguments. They understand supply lines, choke valleys, and the spiritual value of making your enemies climb tired. If a mountain matters, they intend to own the meaning of it.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Athletics.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Logistics OPs.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — The World (Integrator)

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Investigation and Insight.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

system.flavor: He looked her in the eye. He chose the mark.

manifestation.concept: Compel a target to bear witness — to either speak the truth on a chosen subject or carry a visible mark indicating their refusal.
manifestation.riskText: If the target answers truthfully and the truth is dangerous to you, you cannot un-hear it.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can compel speech. Or compel silence-with-consequence. The target chooses which.
manifestation.gmCalibration: T2 Working. Excellent for diplomacy, interrogation, and testimony. Politically loud.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Target must answer one question truthfully or accept the Marked condition (visible to all Pactkeepers, contracts, and institutional structures) for 1d4 sessions.
manifestation.signature: A small invisible sigil affixes to their throat. Visible to other Pactkeepers and to anyone with second sight.
manifestation.thirdThing: The mark of refusal is recognized by every Pactkeeper they meet for a season. Their reputation will travel.

system.flavor: She named the treaty. He sat down.

manifestation.concept: Reach into the record of past agreements and force reality to honor one of them again, here, now.
manifestation.durationText: Until the cited clause is fulfilled or broken.
manifestation.riskText: If you cite a precedent that does not actually exist, the working backfires — 1d4 Stress and the room knows you tried to lie about a contract.
manifestation.pathResonance: Pactkeeper (Archivist) — past rulings as present force.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can hold someone to something they actually agreed to. Reality cooperates.
manifestation.gmCalibration: T1 Working. GM may negotiate the strength of the precedent. Strong precedents = strong compulsion.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Name a precedent — a vow, a treaty, a contract, a rule of the house — that the target has previously agreed to, even implicitly. They must obey it now. If they refuse, they take 1 Blood Debt.
manifestation.signature: A faint sound of a gavel, a sealed envelope tearing, or a bell once rung.
manifestation.thirdThing: The cited precedent is briefly visible to all present — a word, a date, a name. Some of them recognize it.

system.effect: Lift a lantern made of visible obligation. Hidden prices smoke into view; promises gain weight; breaches stop pretending they are misunderstandings.
system.flavor: Gray-gold fire hangs in the lantern like lawful weather.

manifestation.concept: An illuminated clause-space in which agreements reveal their teeth.
manifestation.costText: 1 Clarity to light it; a named agreement, bargain, or expectation must already exist.
manifestation.durationText: So long as the lantern is carried or set between the parties.
manifestation.triggerText: If a clause is broken inside its light, the breach becomes undeniable.
manifestation.targetText: One bargain, one negotiation, one accused lie, or one roomful of obligations.
manifestation.rangeAreaText: Near; room-sized if everyone can see the light.
manifestation.riskText: The lantern is always heaviest for the least honest person present—and sometimes that is you.
manifestation.pathResonance: Pactkeeper / Steward or Auditor doctrine / preserve trust, expose cost, enforce consequence.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can expose hidden terms, mark breach, clarify duty, and make agreements materially real.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Excellent truth-pressure tool. Keep it tied to real obligations, not omniscience.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Scene tool for contract revelation, lie-pressure, and breach consequence.
manifestation.signature: Each live promise appears as a filament of gray-gold fire inside the lantern.
manifestation.thirdThing: The lantern gains weight according to who in the room is least honest.

system.flavor: He opened the field. Everyone realized at once who had been lying for the last three weeks.

manifestation.concept: A circle drawn — physically or implicitly — within which everyone speaks in turn, hears every other voice clearly, and cannot lie without their voice cracking.
manifestation.durationText: While you remain present and willing to enforce the field.
manifestation.riskText: You cannot lie inside the field either. Truths you would rather have not said may surface.
manifestation.pathResonance: Harmony Marshal — the room governed by being heard.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can stop a brawl, expose a fraud, or force a conversation that has been overdue for a decade.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-3 Form. Excellent for diplomatic scenes. Catastrophic in crowded markets, courts, or households with skeletons in the closet.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: While active, no one in the field can take a hostile action without it being seen by everyone present. Lies are exposed (a small but unmistakable cough). All Insight rolls in the field reroll the lowest die.
manifestation.signature: Inside the field, ambient noise drops to a hush. People can hear themselves think. Some find this terrifying.
manifestation.thirdThing: Anyone who lies inside the field is marked: they cough at the moment of the lie. Other people in the field hear it and know.

system.flavor: She set the ledger on the table. She did not need to open it. He withdrew the offer.

manifestation.concept: A ledger — physical or implied — that records every promise spoken near you. The book updates itself. It is impossible to write in falsely.
manifestation.durationText: Persistent. The ledger is a campaign-relevant artifact.
manifestation.riskText: Other Pactkeepers, archivists, and major faction lawyers will want to read it. Some will pay. Some will threaten.
manifestation.pathResonance: Pactkeeper (Archivist) — the long memory of the office.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You have a book that nobody can lie to. Including you.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-3 Form. Strategic-tier item. Excellent for long-arc political play.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Once per session, consult the ledger about a recent promise made in your presence. The ledger names the promise verbatim, the promiser, and any clauses.
manifestation.signature: Pages turn at quiet moments without being touched. Ink gathers on the page like dew.
manifestation.thirdThing: Over a season, the ledger accumulates enough material to embarrass any institution that has lied to you.

system.flavor: She had heard him swear. When he lied, the lie cut him.

manifestation.concept: When an oath sworn in your presence is broken, the breaker takes the wound the oath promised them.
manifestation.durationText: Resolves at the moment of breaking.
manifestation.riskText: Reality charges interest. If the oath was vague, the penalty may be misapplied. If it was specific, the penalty is exact.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can make an oath bite back when it is broken. Witnessed oaths are not free.
manifestation.gmCalibration: T1 Working. Requires you to have witnessed the oath. Conditional but devastating when triggered.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Reaction: when a creature within Near range breaks an oath sworn in your witness, deal 2d6 psychic damage and apply a condition appropriate to the broken oath.
manifestation.signature: A faint snap of a sealed scroll. The breaker visibly winces.
manifestation.thirdThing: The wound is the wound the breaker themselves named when they swore. Reality pays out exactly what was promised.

system.flavor: He buttoned the robe. He had not lied since the year he forged it.

manifestation.concept: A worn vestment — robe, sash, ring — into which you have hammered an oath you keep to yourself. While you wear it, your word carries weight.
manifestation.durationText: Bound to you while you keep the oath.
manifestation.riskText: Breaking the oath costs 1 Blood Debt and the vestment is ruined. Other Pactkeepers will know.
manifestation.pathResonance: Pactkeeper (Steward) — the sworn life made tactile.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You are recognized as a person whose word counts. Until you break it.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-1 Form. The oath must be specific and named at forging. GM enforces.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: +2 to social rolls when you give your word. Once per scene, when you make a promise, all parties present recognize it as binding without requiring further ceremony.
manifestation.signature: The garment is plain but absolutely clean — it does not stain, fray, or weather.
manifestation.thirdThing: If you break the oath, the garment changes — visibly. The change is recognized by every Pactkeeper.

system.effect: Two-handed, heavy. Pairs well with Bulwark Frame.
system.flavor: Not subtle. Not trying to be.

item.signature: When the door is the problem, the maul is the answer.
item.lore:
Two-handed iron-headed maul on a long ash haft. Heavy, slow, and absolutely uninterested in your finesse. The Bulwark's first real weapon — the one you swing when subtlety has already failed.

Standard Issue. Heavy two-handed kinetic. No signature — Frame Dice and Ruin Charges still do their work; the maul just makes the impact mean it.

damageRoll.flavor: Reduce incoming damage by rolled total

manifestation.concept: A spell blocking a certain amount of damage as a reaction
manifestation.signature: Has to be spoken in a monotone voice
manifestation.thirdThing: A booming angry voice echo's behind the PC

manifestation.concept: Manifestation of a shield that buffs AC
